newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Omnitel confirms 589 bln lire loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Omnitel confirms 589 bln lire loss in 1996.

text.p: Italy's second GSM mobile phone service operator Omnitel Pronto Italia confirmed it made a loss, as expected, of 589 billion lire after tax in 1996 on a turnover of 749 billion.

Omnitel Pronto Italia, in which information technology group Olivetti has a 35.49 percent stake, said its investments for 1996 were 729 billion, taking total investments by December 31, 1996 to 2.511 trillion lire including the 750 billion lire payment made for its licence to run the service.
Omnitel said in a statement the commercial trend in the first few months of 1997 was higher than forecast regarding the number of subscribers and the number of sales of a new rechargeable pay card.
Omnitel managing director Silvio Scaglia was quoted in the statement as saying Omnitel also expected it would soon have one million clients, compared with 713,000 at the end of December 1996.

Omnitel, which is controlled by two international consortiums that include Bell Atlantic, Germany's Mannesmann and Airtouch, confirmed it had 28 percent of the market for new subscribers to cellular telephone services and 33 percent of the market for GSM phone services in Italy.
It said territorial coverage in Italy at the end of 1996 was 60 percent, which corresponded to 86 percent of the population.
